title: Random-looking yet repeatable fluid flows should be producible

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Random-looking yet repeatable fluid flows should be producible

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because turbulent randomness is generated intrinsically by large-scale motion, carefully prepared experiments should produce fluid flows that look random yet are essentially the same on every repeated run.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: with sufficiently careful preparation it should be possible to produce patterns of flow that seem quite random but that are nevertheless effectively repeatable—so that they look essentially the same on every successive run of an experiment.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Fluid Flow” (from p. 376), p. 382. Scope: laboratory fluid flows at turbulent or near-turbulent conditions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-09: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.51

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction admits a clean repeated-experiment test with strong discriminating power. Public databases predominantly provide single experiments or simulations, not the required replicated physical runs under carefully matched conditions. New laboratory data are therefore needed.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Repeat a turbulent-flow experiment from independently reset initial conditions, quantify apparent randomness using preregistered statistics, and measure spatial-temporal similarity across runs. Random-looking patterns with reproducibility far above a stochastic-input baseline support the prediction; ordinary run-to-run divergence refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Effective repeatability needs spatial, temporal, and tolerance definitions.

Residual preparation differences may dominate chaotic divergence.

Existing turbulence archives rarely contain independently repeated, meticulously reset runs.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.88
data adequacy: 0.18
discriminating power: 0.78
data existence: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction has a clear statistic: repeatability conditional on looking random. Experiments on a few vortices show repeatable intricate flow, which covers a weaker regime than the one claimed. Open archives of matched turbulent repeats that still look random are not available, so the prediction as stated is only partly tested.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Repeat a carefully prepared flow and compute the cross-run correlation of the velocity field in a regime whose single-run statistics pass randomness tests. High correlation despite random-looking statistics would support the prediction; correlation that collapses as soon as the flow looks random would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Published repeatable flows are mostly regular vortex wakes, not flows that pass randomness tests.

Matched initial conditions at turbulent Reynolds numbers are rarely archived as an open dataset.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.8
data existence: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.65
